facts.claim: "Summertime" is the lead single from Amanda Shires and Bobbie Nelson's collaborative album Loving You, which came out June 23, 2023 on Silver Knife/ATO Records. Willie Nelson sings on the track.
The song is a cover of George Gershwin's "Summertime." Willie Nelson, Bobbie's younger brother, guests on vocals.
The album was produced by Lawrence Rothman and Amanda Shires. Bobbie Nelson plays piano, and Shires sings and plays fiddle. Willie Nelson sings on track 4, "Summertime."

The "Summertime" video was co-directed by Shires and Deren Ney. It was filmed during the album sessions at Arlyn Studios in Austin, Texas. Arlyn is run by Bobbie's son Freddy Fletcher, who also played drums on the album.
Shires said Bobbie Nelson died on March 10, 2022, just months after the two spent 6 days together in Austin recording the album.
Shires said Bobbie related to the song because she was a mother and the family unit was important to her, whether or not she had the idealized version.
Shires recalled that after the two agreed to make a whole record, Bobbie said the next song would be "Summertime."
Bobbie and Willie Nelson had already recorded "Summertime" for Willie's Grammy-winning 2016 album Summertime: Willie Nelson Sings Gershwin.

The album grew out of the sessions for Shires' 2022 solo album Take It Like a Man. She booked studio time with Bobbie for "Always on My Mind" because "the only piano that fits that song is Bobbie's." They then decided to make a full album together.
Consequence described the track as giving the jazz standard a southern twang, with Shires' fiddle over Bobbie's piano and Shires' bright soprano set against Willie's deep voice.

research.lineage: The track sits in the Texas country/Americana tradition, reworking a Gershwin jazz standard in the Nelson family's blend of country, gospel and standards.

draft:
In **Summertime**, a fiddle holds long notes and slips short fills between the sung lines, fingerpicked acoustic guitar rolls underneath, and a walking bass steps along at a slow, swaying pace. Bobbie Nelson's piano lays down plain, steady chords. The room is open and a little reverberant, and everything is clean, unhurried and close. It sounds like a lullaby because it is one. By the time anyone heard it, the woman at the piano was gone.

Amanda Shires and Bobbie Nelson spent six days together in Austin making the album *Loving You*, and Bobbie died on March 10, 2022, a few months later. The record started almost by accident. During the sessions for Shires' *Take It Like a Man*, Shires booked time with Bobbie for "Always on My Mind" because, as she put it, "the only piano that fits that song is Bobbie's." Once they agreed to make a whole album, Shires recalled, Bobbie named the next song herself: "Summertime." She'd already cut it with her younger brother Willie for his Gershwin record, *Summertime: Willie Nelson Sings Gershwin*. Here Willie comes back to sing on it again, so the Nelson siblings' long habit of treating jazz standards like country and gospel hymns gets one more pass.

Gershwin's lyric is a promise no parent can fully keep. "So hush, little baby" is the job of a lullaby: calm the child, make the world sound safe. The second verse carries the real weight. The child will someday "take to the sky," but until then, nothing will harm them, "Not with your daddy and your mama / Standin' by." Shires said Bobbie loved the song because she was a mother and family mattered to her, "whether or not she had the idealized version." That clause is the key. The song describes a home where daddy's rich and mama's good-looking, and it's sung by people who know homes rarely look like that. The comfort isn't a lie. It's a wish said out loud on behalf of someone smaller.

The voices carry that double feeling. Shires' bright soprano, clear and smooth, sits against Willie's deep voice, and the harmonies settle in warmly on the phrases they share. Nobody pushes. The arrangement never builds, and the song ends the way lullabies end, circling "the livin' is easy" until it lands back on "don't you cry." The sessions happened at Arlyn Studios, which is run by Bobbie's son, Freddy Fletcher. So the family really was standing by while it was made.

The song gets to you because it's a promise of protection sung by someone who won't be there to keep it, and the tenderness doesn't waver at all.
